verdict.rationale: USPTO publishes a sign-in path requiring a USPTO.gov account with multifactor authentication plus a one-time identity verification that 'can be completed online in less than 15 minutes', so a human can complete it remotely without an in-person visit. A paper verification path is offered as an option, not a requirement. The evidence does not say how the online identity check works, so it may rely on biometric liveness (selfie/ID matching), which this story excludes. missing for 10: documentation of the online identity-verification method (confirming no biometric liveness or mailed PIN), the specific MFA factors supported, and hands-on or independent corroboration of remote completion.

support.subject: As an AI-native founder, the published sign-in path is credential MFA an authorized human can complete remotely — not biometric liveness, an in-person visit, or a PIN by physical mail

citations.quote: create a USPTO.gov account with multifactor authentication methods and verify your identity before you can log in to access TEAS and Trademark Center.
this one-time verification process can be completed online in less than 15 minutes.
